new_statements.quote: Occitan has contrastive lexical stress, falling either on the last or the penult syllable (Meisenburg 2001; Schultz-Gora 1906). For example, the word pati [ˈpa.ti] (‘patio’) with penult stress contrasts with patir [pa.ˈti] (‘to suffer’) with final stress. In this sense, it resembles the majority of Romance languages, yet antepenultimate stress is not attested in the majority of Occitan dialects. Words ending in a consonant — except morphological -n and -s — are generally stress-final, but words ending in a vowel may be stressed either on the final or on the penultimate syllable.
new_statements.citation: Sichel-Bazin, Rafèu. 2015. Prosodic systems in contact: Occitan and French. PhD thesis, Universität Osnabrück / Universitat Pompeu Fabra (supervisors Trudel Meisenburg, Pilar Prieto). 493 pp. Open access: https://core.ac.uk/download/hdl 10803/321597).
new_statements.locator: §3.2.2.3 'Word stress in Occitan', p. 103 (printed page = PDF page 103); footnote markers 16 and 17 omitted from the quote (fn.16: antepenultimate stress only in Niçart, Vivaroalpine of Italy and colloquial Aranese; fn.17: few exceptions such as nívol [ˈni.βul] 'cloud'). Supporting: p. 56 'default pattern: stress on the last syllable if it is closed by a consonant, otherwise on the penult'; p. 20 fn. 4 states the examples are central Lengadocian, the dialect used as general standard.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is confined to the last two syllables. Words ending in a consonant other than inflectional -n/-s take final stress (in Languedocien the final consonant is treated as the onset of an empty-nucleus syllable licensed by the stressed foot: Sauzet 2004 p.5 'Les mots à segment final supposé former une attaque ont tous l'accent sur la syllabe finale'). Vowel-final words are penultimate by default but may be lexically final (contrastive pairs pati/patir, sabon 'they know'/sabon 'soap'), so the weight rule is overlaid by lexical marking of vowel-final oxytones; no antepenultimate stress in Languedocien.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed in the word-stress section (the dissertation treats phrase-level accentual phrases separately).
new_statements.exceptions: Consonant-final paroxytones are rare and mostly inflectional (-n, -s) or a few lexical items such as nívol 'cloud', which tend to drop the consonant or shift stress; antepenultimate stress only in peripheral Niçart, Cisalpine and colloquial Aranese (not Languedocien); loans keep source-language stress unless impossible, popular usage stresses loans finally (p.56); Lemosin has a separate weight-sensitive system (not Languedocien).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (lexical stress, citation forms and dictionary forms); the rule is stated for Occitan generally, with central Lengadocian as the reference variety of the dissertation (Lacaune, Tarn, corpus and examples); Sauzet 2004 p.5 states the final-consonant condition specifically for 'languedocien occidental'.
new_statements.identity_note: lang1334 is a Glottolog 5.1 bookkeeping node for retired ISO 639-3 code lnc (Languedocien, merged into oci in 2007); the living Glottolog node is the dialect Languedocian Occitan lang1309 (Southern Occitan sout2612 < Occitan occi1239), with subdialects Bas-Languedocien basl1241, Haut-Languedocien haut1244 and Languedocien Moyen lang1310. The deciding source describes Occitan with central Lengadocian (Lacaune, Tarn) as its reference variety; the supporting Sauzet 2004 statement is for western Languedocien. Occitan occi1239 is already in the catalog (weight-hedged, Wheeler 1988:251), so this would be a dialect-level entry under it.

sources.quote: Occitan has contrastive lexical stress, falling either on the last or the penult syllable (Meisenburg 2001; Schultz-Gora 1906). For example, the word pati [ˈpa.ti] (‘patio’) with penult stress contrasts with patir [pa.ˈti] (‘to suffer’) with final stress. In this sense, it resembles the majority of Romance languages, yet antepenultimate stress is not attested in the majority of Occitan dialects. sources.locator: §3.2.2.3 'Word stress in Occitan', p. 103 (printed page = PDF page 103); footnote markers 16 and 17 omitted from the quote (fn.16: antepenultimate stress only in Niçart, Vivaroalpine of Italy and colloquial Aranese; fn.17: few exceptions such as nívol [ˈni.βul] 'cloud'). Supporting: p. 56 'default pattern: stress on the last syllable if it is closed by a consonant, otherwise on the penult'; p. 20 fn. 4 states the examples are central Lengadocian, the dialect used as general standard.
sources.note: §3.2.2.3 'Word stress in Occitan' p.103: contrastive lexical stress on final or penult (pati vs patir); consonant-final words (except inflectional -n, -s) generally stress-final, vowel-final words final or penult; no antepenult except Niçart, Cisalpine, colloquial Aranese (fn.16); fn.17 rare exceptions like nívol. p.56: default pattern 'stress on the last syllable if it is closed by a consonant, otherwise on the penult'. Examples and corpus are central Lengadocian (Lacaune, Tarn), which the author uses as the standard (p.20 fn.4).

sources.note: p.2: 'L'occitan accentue la syllabe finale ou la pénultième', minimal pair sabon [ˈsabu(n)] 'they know' vs sabon [saˈbu(n)] 'soap'; plural -s in Limousin can shift stress (not Languedocien).

sources.citation: Sauzet, Patrick. 2001 [2004]. Variation des finales occitanes et format de la syllabe. HAL preprint halshs-00390058.
sources.note: p.5: 'L'occitan accentue la fin du mot : la syllabe finale ou la pénultième. Les mots à segment final supposé former une attaque ont tous l'accent sur la syllabe finale'; a final empty-nucleus syllable is licensed 'en languedocien occidental si elle forme la partie faible du pied final' (left-headed final foot). Explicitly about western Languedocien (lang. occ.) vs eastern Languedocien and Provençal.

sources.note: p.251 'Stress': Occitan shuns proparoxytones except Nice/Italy; consonant-final paroxytones rare unless the final consonant is inflectional; this is the catalog's deciding source for occi1239 (weight-hedged).
